## Abstract

The spider genus Desis Walckenaer, 1837 is the type genus of the spider family Desidae Pocock, 1895. Desis spiders hide in silk sacs between rocks or shells during high tide and forage during low tide (Baehr et al. 2017). Four Desis species have been recorded from Asia: Desis gardineri Pocock, 1904 (India), Desis inermis Gravely, 1927 (India), Desis japonica Yaginuma, 1956 (Japan) and Desis martensi L. Koch, 1872 (Malaysia) (World Spider Catalog 2020). Until now, only one species of the family Desidae, Badumna tangae Zhu, Zhang Yang, 2006, has been reported from China (Zhu et al. 2006). Here, we describe a new species of Desis and report the genus from China for the first time.

## Abstract

The spider genus Desis Walckenaer, 1837 is the type genus of the spider family Desidae Pocock, 1895. Desis spiders hide in silk sacs between rocks or shells during high tide and forage during low tide (Baehr et al. 2017). Four Desis species have been recorded from Asia: Desis gardineri Pocock, 1904 (India), Desis inermis Gravely, 1927 (India), Desis japonica Yaginuma, 1956 (Japan) and Desis martensi L. Koch, 1872 (Malaysia) (World Spider Catalog 2020). Until now, only one species of the family Desidae, Badumna tangae Zhu, Zhang Yang, 2006, has been reported from China (Zhu et al. 2006). Here, we describe a new species of Desis and report the genus from China for the first time.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

**Desidae** is a family of [spiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider "Spider"), some of which are known as **intertidal spiders**. The family is named for the genus _[Desis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desis\_(spider) "Desis (spider)")_, members of which inhabit the [intertidal zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intertidal_zone "Intertidal zone"). The family has been reevaluated in recent years and now includes inland genera and species as well, such as _[Badumna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badumna "Badumna")_ and _[Phryganoporus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phryganoporus "Phryganoporus")_. The vast majority of genera currently included in Desidae are native to [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"), [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand"), or [New Caledonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Caledonia "New Caledonia"), although some are found in other parts of the world.

In 2017, the family Amphinectidae was merged into Desidae and the family [Toxopidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxopidae "Toxopidae") was separated from it.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-wheeler-1) Those intertidal spiders that are truly marine commonly live in [barnacle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnacle "Barnacle") shells, which they seal up with silk; this allows them to maintain an air bubble during high tide. They emerge at night to feed on various small [arthropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod "Arthropod") that live in the intertidal zone.

## Distribution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Desidae&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Distribution")]

As now [circumscribed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumscription_(taxonomy) "Circumscription (taxonomy)"), the family Desidae is mainly found in [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and [Australasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australasia "Australasia"), with some species reaching north to [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-wsc-2)

_[Metaltella simoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaltella\_simoni "Metaltella simoni")_ has been introduced in a large part of the Southern United States (records exist from [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi"), and [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida")). It is feared that it could [extirpate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_extinction "Local extinction") the native [titanoecid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanoecidae "Titanoecidae") species _[Titanoeca brunnea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanoeca\_brunnea "Titanoeca brunnea")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-edwards-3)

**Desidae** is a family of [spiders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider "Spider"), some of which are known as **intertidal spiders**. The family is named for the genus _[Desis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desis\_(spider) "Desis (spider)")_, members of which inhabit the [intertidal zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intertidal_zone "Intertidal zone"). The family has been reevaluated in recent years and now includes inland genera and species as well, such as _[Badumna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badumna "Badumna")_ and _[Phryganoporus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phryganoporus "Phryganoporus")_. The vast majority of genera currently included in Desidae are native to [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"), [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand"), or [New Caledonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Caledonia "New Caledonia"), although some are found in other parts of the world.

In 2017, the family Amphinectidae was merged into Desidae and the family [Toxopidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxopidae "Toxopidae") was separated from it.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-wheeler-1) Those intertidal spiders that are truly marine commonly live in [barnacle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnacle "Barnacle") shells, which they seal up with silk; this allows them to maintain an air bubble during high tide. They emerge at night to feed on various small [arthropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod "Arthropod") that live in the intertidal zone.

## Distribution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Desidae&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Distribution")]

As now [circumscribed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumscription_(taxonomy) "Circumscription (taxonomy)"), the family Desidae is mainly found in [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and [Australasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australasia "Australasia"), with some species reaching north to [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-wsc-2)

_[Metaltella simoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaltella\_simoni "Metaltella simoni")_ has been introduced in a large part of the Southern United States (records exist from [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), [Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana "Louisiana"), [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi "Mississippi"), and [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida")). It is feared that it could [extirpate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_extinction "Local extinction") the native [titanoecid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanoecidae "Titanoecidae") species _[Titanoeca brunnea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanoeca\_brunnea "Titanoeca brunnea")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desidae#cite_note-edwards-3)

### [Arachnida • 2020] _Desis jiaxiangi_• First Report of the Spider Genus _Desis_ (Araneae, Desidae) from China, with Description of A New Species

  

[![Image 1](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgYCaGuDWbGdwujnQbs6lZDZBLQgiWm7w9ehYzKTwsGgwKNcmuyHjHbQzhFltGobL7uBzlD4ZcaCfHcuK4xXTOO0V6Fqjy4Amf2DuLQWQI9kuIQaSS5NSFblHIbbPZlibYCwY7PHFYR7kUO/s400/Desis_jiaxiangi-novataxa_2020-Lin_Li_et_Chen.jpg)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgYCaGuDWbGdwujnQbs6lZDZBLQgiWm7w9ehYzKTwsGgwKNcmuyHjHbQzhFltGobL7uBzlD4ZcaCfHcuK4xXTOO0V6Fqjy4Amf2DuLQWQI9kuIQaSS5NSFblHIbbPZlibYCwY7PHFYR7kUO/s1600/Desis_jiaxiangi-novataxa_2020-Lin_Li_et_Chen.jpg)
**_Desis jiaxiangi_**Lin, Li & Chen, 2020  

  
DOI:[_10.11646/zootaxa.4755.3.11_](https://doi.org/10.11646/zootaxa.4755.3.11)  
Photograph by Zixuan Lin.

  

 The spider genus _Desis_ Walckenaer, 1837 is the type genus of the spider family Desidae Pocock, 1895. _Desis_ spiders hide in silk sacs between rocks or shells during high tide and forage during low tide (Baehr et al. 2017). Four _Desis_ species have been recorded from Asia: _Desis gardineri_ Pocock, 1904 (India), _Desis inermis_ Gravely, 1927 (India), _Desis japonica_ Yaginuma, 1956 (Japan) and _Desis martensi_ L. Koch, 1872 (Malaysia) (World Spider Catalog 2020). Until now, only one species of the family Desidae, _Badumna tangae_ Zhu, Zhang & Yang, 2006, has been reported from China (Zhu _et al_. 2006). Here, we describe **a new species** of _Desis_ and report the genus from China for the first time.

  

[![Image 2](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgqY-gBdK-aNTUnIf-myCbnHXoqptWBy9UYr5yPJJ_1EEWn6uamB0ui-uuJXxJ3NtyizDBc3X99NfEAJU_Q5B2YI9FnUT0WSqFjlwSOoh_R-f8MzUPUjp4mmnbNeHyq7dzwsB776NtpPzVS/s400/Desis_jiaxiangi-novataxa_2020-Lin_Li_et_Chen.jpg)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgqY-gBdK-aNTUnIf-myCbnHXoqptWBy9UYr5yPJJ_1EEWn6uamB0ui-uuJXxJ3NtyizDBc3X99NfEAJU_Q5B2YI9FnUT0WSqFjlwSOoh_R-f8MzUPUjp4mmnbNeHyq7dzwsB776NtpPzVS/s1600/Desis_jiaxiangi-novataxa_2020-Lin_Li_et_Chen.jpg)
**Figure 4._Desis jiaxiangi_**, live holotype male.  

 Photograph by Zixuan Lin.

  

**_Desis jiaxiangi_ sp. nov.**

  

**Etymology.**The species is named after Mr **Jiaxiang Wu**, the collector of the holotype; noun (name) in genitive case.

### [Arachnida • 2020] _Desis jiaxiangi_• First Report of the Spider Genus _Desis_ (Araneae, Desidae) from China, with Description of A New Species

  

[![Image 1](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgYCaGuDWbGdwujnQbs6lZDZBLQgiWm7w9ehYzKTwsGgwKNcmuyHjHbQzhFltGobL7uBzlD4ZcaCfHcuK4xXTOO0V6Fqjy4Amf2DuLQWQI9kuIQaSS5NSFblHIbbPZlibYCwY7PHFYR7kUO/s400/Desis_jiaxiangi-novataxa_2020-Lin_Li_et_Chen.jpg)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgYCaGuDWbGdwujnQbs6lZDZBLQgiWm7w9ehYzKTwsGgwKNcmuyHjHbQzhFltGobL7uBzlD4ZcaCfHcuK4xXTOO0V6Fqjy4Amf2DuLQWQI9kuIQaSS5NSFblHIbbPZlibYCwY7PHFYR7kUO/s1600/Desis_jiaxiangi-novataxa_2020-Lin_Li_et_Chen.jpg)
**_Desis jiaxiangi_**Lin, Li & Chen, 2020  

  
DOI:[_10.11646/zootaxa.4755.3.11_](https://doi.org/10.11646/zootaxa.4755.3.11)  
Photograph by Zixuan Lin.

  

 The spider genus _Desis_ Walckenaer, 1837 is the type genus of the spider family Desidae Pocock, 1895. _Desis_ spiders hide in silk sacs between rocks or shells during high tide and forage during low tide (Baehr et al. 2017). Four _Desis_ species have been recorded from Asia: _Desis gardineri_ Pocock, 1904 (India), _Desis inermis_ Gravely, 1927 (India), _Desis japonica_ Yaginuma, 1956 (Japan) and _Desis martensi_ L. Koch, 1872 (Malaysia) (World Spider Catalog 2020). Until now, only one species of the family Desidae, _Badumna tangae_ Zhu, Zhang & Yang, 2006, has been reported from China (Zhu _et al_. 2006). Here, we describe **a new species** of _Desis_ and report the genus from China for the first time.

  

[![Image 2](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgqY-gBdK-aNTUnIf-myCbnHXoqptWBy9UYr5yPJJ_1EEWn6uamB0ui-uuJXxJ3NtyizDBc3X99NfEAJU_Q5B2YI9FnUT0WSqFjlwSOoh_R-f8MzUPUjp4mmnbNeHyq7dzwsB776NtpPzVS/s400/Desis_jiaxiangi-novataxa_2020-Lin_Li_et_Chen.jpg)](https://blogger.googleusercontent.com/img/b/R29vZ2xl/AVvXsEgqY-gBdK-aNTUnIf-myCbnHXoqptWBy9UYr5yPJJ_1EEWn6uamB0ui-uuJXxJ3NtyizDBc3X99NfEAJU_Q5B2YI9FnUT0WSqFjlwSOoh_R-f8MzUPUjp4mmnbNeHyq7dzwsB776NtpPzVS/s1600/Desis_jiaxiangi-novataxa_2020-Lin_Li_et_Chen.jpg)

 Photograph by Zixuan Lin.

  

**_Desis jiaxiangi_ sp. nov.**

  

**Etymology.**The species is named after Mr **Jiaxiang Wu**, the collector of the holotype; noun (name) in genitive case.
